item.text:
{
  "schema_version": "evidence-intents-v1",
  "source_id": "MAC-010",
  "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
  "draft_intents": [
    {
      "draft_id": "D0001",
      "intent": "Mexico's current administration pursued a policy agenda combining redistribution, trade promotion, infrastructure investment, and trade integration, with stated aims of fostering development, especially in southern states.",
      "actor": "Mexico's current administration",
      "action": "Pursued a policy agenda",
      "mechanism": "Redistribution, trade promotion, infrastructure investment, and trade integration",
      "outcome": "Aimed to foster development, especially in southern states",
      "date_or_period": "Current administration as assessed in the 2022 Article IV report",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period; the passage does not identify the ruler by name.",
      "limitations": "The passage describes the agenda and its aims, not complete implementation or realized outcomes.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0002",
      "intent": "The administration implemented or advanced the USMCA, increased the minimum wage, enacted a subcontracting law, increased the general social pension, and developed trade infrastructure in the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.",
      "actor": "Mexico's current administration",
      "action": "Implemented or advanced flagship reforms and infrastructure development",
      "mechanism": "USMCA implementation; minimum-wage increases; subcontracting law; general social-pension increases; Isthmus corridor development",
      "outcome": "The reforms were intended to reduce wage inequality and old-age poverty and support development; the passage identifies the infrastructure project but does not establish its completed effects.",
      "date_or_period": "By the 2022 Article IV assessment",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff description of flagship reforms",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not quantify implementation quality or realized effects and does not establish whether all measures were fully executed.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.4", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0003",
      "intent": "The IMF assessed that the policy agenda addressed some obstacles to higher productivity and growth but that additional efforts were needed on corruption, crime, rule of law, human capital, infrastructure, and labor and product market rigidities.",
      "actor": "Mexico's current administration and the Mexican policy environment",
      "action": "Addressed some growth constraints but left further policy needs",
      "mechanism": "Redistribution, trade, infrastructure, trade integration, and related reforms, alongside unresolved structural constraints",
      "outcome": "Some obstacles to higher productivity and growth were addressed, while significant impediments remained.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 Article IV assessment",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Directly fits the target assessment period.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not attribute each unresolved issue to a specific decision by the ruler.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.4", "5B.5", "5B.6", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0004",
      "intent": "Mexico's cautious fiscal and monetary policies were associated with moderate inflation, exchange-rate stability, and stable public debt, although productivity growth remained weak despite trade opening and macroeconomic stability.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "Maintained cautious fiscal and monetary policies",
      "mechanism": "Fiscal and monetary policy management in a stable macroeconomic environment",
      "outcome": "Moderate inflation, exchange-rate stability, and stable public debt; productivity gains remained weak.",
      "date_or_period": "Through 2021 or the latest available year, as discussed in the 2022 report",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 Article IV evaluation of the preceding period.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not isolate the ruler's personal role or establish causality for each outcome.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 26",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0005",
      "intent": "Mexico's financial system emerged from the pandemic with low and declining non-performing loans, high and rising capital adequacy ratios, comfortable liquidity ratios, and resilience in severe macrofinancial stress tests, although some smaller banks might need additional buffers.",
      "actor": "Mexican financial system and authorities",
      "action": "Maintained or operated a resilient financial system",
      "mechanism": "Capital and liquidity buffers, low private-sector leverage, and financial supervision",
      "outcome": "Systemic vulnerabilities and liquidity risks appeared broadly contained; some smaller banks may require additional buffers under severe stress.",
      "date_or_period": "Pandemic aftermath and 2022 FSAP",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF assessment based on 2022 FSAP stress tests",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "This is a system-level assessment and does not establish the ruler's appointment, policy, or compliance decisions.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 23",
      "start_segment_id": "S00003",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0006",
      "intent": "Mexican authorities rolled out Basel reforms, including Total Loss Absorbing Capacity requirements and improved supervisory techniques, while the IMF recommended strengthening regulatory-agency autonomy, resources, and supervisors' legal protection.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities and IMF",
      "action": "Implemented selected financial reforms; recommended further institutional strengthening",
      "mechanism": "Basel reforms, TLAC requirements, supervisory techniques, regulatory-agency autonomy, resources, and legal protections",
      "outcome": "Financial-system resilience was supported, but regulatory capacity and independence required further strengthening.",
      "date_or_period": "By 2022",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment and recommendations",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 Article IV and FSAP assessment.",
      "limitations": "The recommendation to strengthen autonomy and resources is prospective and does not prove that the ruler failed to appoint or empower qualified professionals.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.3", "5B.7"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 24",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00003"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0007",
      "intent": "The IMF reported that Mexico's authorities had undertaken efforts to increase access to bank branches and financial products, improve transparency, broaden access through digital connectivity, and develop Fintech competition and inclusion.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "Undertook financial-deepening and inclusion efforts",
      "mechanism": "Expanded branch and product access, digital connectivity, and the 2018 Fintech law",
      "outcome": "The Fintech law helped foster rapid creation of new firms, primarily in e-payments; financial inclusion and competition were policy objectives.",
      "date_or_period": "Recent years through 2022; the Fintech law dates from 2018",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period, with one reform dated to 2018.",
      "limitations": "The IMF also described Mexico's financial depth as relatively poor and called for continued efforts; the passage does not establish the ruler's personal role.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 25",
      "start_segment_id": "S00003",
      "end_segment_id": "S00007"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0008",
      "intent": "The authorities' agenda included establishing a beneficial-ownership register and strengthening AML/CFT supervision, resources, enforcement, and sanctions, but the IMF stated that effectiveness still needed to be enhanced.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities",
      "action": "Developed and strengthened financial-integrity rules and institutions",
      "mechanism": "Beneficial-ownership information and register, consolidated supervision, resources, enforcement, and proportionate, consistent, dissuasive sanctions",
      "outcome": "The legal and regulatory framework had made good progress toward FATF alignment, while effective implementation remained incomplete.",
      "date_or_period": "By 2022",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "The passage describes plans and needed improvements rather than verified enforcement against specific politically connected actors.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.5", "5B.7"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 25",
      "start_segment_id": "S00010",
      "end_segment_id": "S00014"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0009",
      "intent": "The authorities stated that supervisors and regulators had a track record of operating with a high level of independence, while acknowledging that the institutional arrangements governing regulatory-agency autonomy were defined legislatively.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities, supervisors, and regulators",
      "action": "Reported and maintained regulatory independence",
      "mechanism": "Legislatively defined institutional arrangements and supervisory practice",
      "outcome": "Authorities characterized regulatory supervisors and regulators as operating with high independence.",
      "date_or_period": "As of the 2022 Article IV consultation",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "Authorities' views as reported by the IMF",
      "period_fit": "Directly fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "This is an attributed official view, not an independent IMF verification; it does not address appointment qualifications, selection processes, or performance-based retention.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.2", "5B.7"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 26",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00002"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0010",
      "intent": "Mexico's poverty rate remained around 40 percent, rose in 2020 during the pandemic, and subsequently fell back toward pre-pandemic levels as real income rebounded.",
      "actor": "Mexican population and economy",
      "action": "Experienced pandemic-related poverty deterioration followed by recovery",
      "mechanism": "Pandemic shock and subsequent economic recovery",
      "outcome": "Poverty increased in 2020 and then declined toward its pre-pandemic level.",
      "date_or_period": "2020 through the 2022 assessment",
      "quantities": "Poverty rates hovered around 40 percent",
      "attribution": "IMF staff drawing on CONEVAL data",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 report's recent-period assessment.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not attribute the trajectory to a specific ruler or policy and notes missing 2020Q2 income-survey data elsewhere in the same section.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 27",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00002"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0011",
      "intent": "Mexico had persistent stark regional inequalities: northern and central regions benefited substantially from proximity to the United States, while the south had limited integration and economic opportunity, resulting in lower investment in health, education, and infrastructure and poorer economic performance.",
      "actor": "Mexican regions and national policy environment",
      "action": "Exhibited unequal regional development",
      "mechanism": "Unequal integration, economic opportunity, and investment",
      "outcome": "Southern regions had lower investment, poorer economic performance, and lower real incomes; regional inequalities showed no sign of narrowing.",
      "date_or_period": "As assessed in 2022",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "The evidence describes distributional conditions but does not establish which policies caused them or whether the ruler corrected them.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 27",
      "start_segment_id": "S00003",
      "end_segment_id": "S00005"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0012",
      "intent": "The IMF recommended a gradual permanent increase in government spending of approximately 2 to 3 percent of GDP, financed by tax reform, to promote inclusive growth, reduce poverty, and address pandemic legacies.",
      "actor": "IMF staff and Mexican authorities as policy recipients",
      "action": "Recommended increasing productive public spending and revenue",
      "mechanism": "Permanent spending increase in education, health, public investment, and social safety nets, financed by tax reform",
      "outcome": "Expected to support inclusive growth, reduce poverty, and address pandemic-related effects.",
      "date_or_period": "Recommendation made in the 2022 Article IV report; medium-term implementation",
      "quantities": "Approximately 2–3 percent of GDP in additional annual spending",
      "attribution": "IMF staff recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 policy assessment but is prospective rather than evidence of completed action.",
      "limitations": "This is a recommendation, not proof that the ruler enacted or executed the proposed measures.",
      "polarity": "neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00010",
      "end_segment_id": "S00012"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0013",
      "intent": "The IMF identified spending shortfalls in education, health, public investment, and social safety nets; spending per student, teacher-to-student ratios, and public health spending per capita were below OECD averages and somewhat below emerging-market averages.",
      "actor": "Mexican government and public-service system",
      "action": "Provided comparatively low levels of selected public spending and service inputs",
      "mechanism": "Insufficient education, health, public-investment, and social-safety-net spending",
      "outcome": "Human-capital, health, infrastructure, and social-protection capacity were constrained relative to benchmark countries.",
      "date_or_period": "Pre- and post-pandemic conditions assessed in 2022",
      "quantities": "Below OECD averages and somewhat below emerging-market averages",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment citing IMF and OECD comparisons",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment of structural indicators and pandemic needs.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not establish budget execution quality or attribute the shortfalls solely to the ruler.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.6", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00006",
      "end_segment_id": "S00009"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0014",
      "intent": "The IMF assessed that social-assistance efficiency could be improved by reducing benefit leakage to high-income groups and eliminating overlaps and coverage gaps through a single beneficiary registry.",
      "actor": "Mexican government and social-assistance system",
      "action": "Needed to improve targeting and administrative efficiency",
      "mechanism": "Single beneficiary registry, reduced leakage, and elimination of program overlaps and coverage gaps",
      "outcome": "Potentially more efficient and equitable social assistance",
      "date_or_period": "2022 policy recommendation",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment but is prospective.",
      "limitations": "The passage proposes reforms and does not demonstrate that the ruler implemented them.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.6", "5B.7", "5B.8"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00012",
      "end_segment_id": "S00013"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0015",
      "intent": "Mexican authorities closed expected fiscal gaps in recent years through revenue and spending measures and small changes in the budget-deficit target; IMF staff projected a fiscal gap of 0.2 percent of GDP in 2023 rising to approximately 1.3 percent by 2027.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities and IMF staff",
      "action": "Closed recent expected fiscal gaps and projected future fiscal pressures",
      "mechanism": "Revenue measures, spending measures, and changes to the budget-deficit target",
      "outcome": "Recent expected gaps were closed, but a future fiscal gap was projected to widen.",
      "date_or_period": "Recent years; projections for 2023 and 2027",
      "quantities": "0.2 percent of GDP in 2023; approximately 1.3 percent of GDP by 2027",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment and macroeconomic forecasts",
      "period_fit": "Combines historical assessment with prospective forecasts in the 2022 report.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not specify the ruler's role in each measure or whether the projected gap materialized.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 28",
      "start_segment_id": "S00014",
      "end_segment_id": "S00015"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0016",
      "intent": "The IMF assessed that Pemex restructuring needed to continue, including focusing production on profitable fields, selling non-core assets, reforming its pension scheme, and using more private-sector partnerships to maintain or increase production at lower cost and reduce risks to Pemex and the government budget.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities and Pemex",
      "action": "Needed to continue restructuring Pemex",
      "mechanism": "Profitable-field focus, non-core-asset sales, pension reform, and private upstream partnerships",
      "outcome": "Expected lower costs, maintained or increased production capacity, and reduced fiscal and financial risks.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 assessment; higher oil prices had reduced immediate debt-service pressures",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 Article IV assessment.",
      "limitations": "The passage identifies unfinished reforms and expected benefits rather than completed implementation.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 29",
      "start_segment_id": "S00002",
      "end_segment_id": "S00004"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0017",
      "intent": "Mexico's non-oil revenue was nearly 6 percent of GDP below Latin American peers and about half the OECD average before the pandemic; the IMF stated that tax-policy reform was essential in addition to continued tax-administration strengthening.",
      "actor": "Mexican fiscal authorities",
      "action": "Operated with comparatively low non-oil revenue and needed tax reform",
      "mechanism": "Tax administration and reforms to VAT, personal income, subnational, and carbon taxation",
      "outcome": "Fiscal capacity was weaker than regional and OECD benchmarks, limiting financing for permanent spending increases.",
      "date_or_period": "Before the pandemic; recommendation in 2022",
      "quantities": "Nearly 6 percent of GDP below Latin American peers; about half the OECD average",
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Historical baseline used in the 2022 assessment.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not establish whether the ruler caused the revenue gap or implemented the proposed reforms.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 29",
      "start_segment_id": "S00004",
      "end_segment_id": "S00006"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0018",
      "intent": "The IMF stated that a credible, well-designed medium-term tax reform could finance permanent increases in health, education, and social-assistance spending and recommended measures to broaden tax bases, strengthen audits, and increase selected property, vehicle, and carbon taxes.",
      "actor": "IMF staff and Mexican authorities as policy recipients",
      "action": "Recommended medium-term tax reform",
      "mechanism": "VAT-base changes, personal-income-tax-base expansion, stronger audit and risk management, property and vehicle-tax enforcement, and higher carbon pricing",
      "outcome": "Expected additional revenue to finance public services and investment.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 recommendation; carbon-tax target by 2030",
      "quantities": "Carbon tax described as USD 3 per ton of CO2 and recommended to rise to USD 75 by 2030; possible carbon-tax revenue close to 1.8 percent of GDP by 2030",
      "attribution": "IMF staff recommendation",
      "period_fit": "Prospective recommendation made during the 2022 assessment.",
      "limitations": "The passage does not show enactment, administration, compliance, or distributional incidence of these proposed reforms.",
      "polarity": "neutral",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 29",
      "start_segment_id": "S00005",
      "end_segment_id": "S00015"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0019",
      "intent": "The IMF judged that a comprehensive package of higher spending financed by higher revenues could create positive complementarities between growth and equity, particularly through more efficient productive spending in regions with concentrated socioeconomic gaps and compensation for poor households alongside VAT reforms.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities as prospective policy implementer",
      "action": "Considered or were advised to adopt a growth-and-equity fiscal package",
      "mechanism": "Higher productive spending, higher revenues, regionally targeted investment, VAT reform, and compensation for poor households",
      "outcome": "Expected to improve growth, equity, human capital, and productivity while limiting adverse effects on poor households.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 medium-term policy discussion",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment; authorities expressed support for a productive-spending increase supported by tax reforms",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 assessment; effects were prospective.",
      "limitations": "The package required time to implement, and the passage does not provide completed outcome evidence.",
      "polarity": "positive",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.1", "5B.6", "5B.8", "5B.9", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 30",
      "start_segment_id": "S00001",
      "end_segment_id": "S00008"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0020",
      "intent": "Mexican authorities stated that administrative measures taken by the current administration to combat tax evasion and tax fraud would continue to maintain robust revenues, while acknowledging that the proposed spending and tax measures would require time to implement.",
      "actor": "Mexican authorities and current administration",
      "action": "Reported continued tax-enforcement measures and acknowledged implementation lags",
      "mechanism": "Administrative measures against tax evasion and tax fraud",
      "outcome": "Authorities expected robust revenues in the interim; broader fiscal reforms were not immediate.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 authorities' views",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "Authorities' views as reported by the IMF",
      "period_fit": "Directly fits the 2022 assessment period.",
      "limitations": "The claim about maintaining robust revenues is an official assertion; the passage does not independently verify enforcement results or the ruler's personal supervision.",
      "polarity": "mixed",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.7", "5B.9"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 30",
      "start_segment_id": "S00007",
      "end_segment_id": "S00009"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0021",
      "intent": "The IMF assessed that contract enforcement through civil justice was very weak, discouraging business expansion and formal employment, complicating collateral seizure, and impeding financial development.",
      "actor": "Mexican civil-justice system",
      "action": "Provided weak contract enforcement",
      "mechanism": "Weak civil-justice enforcement and collateral-seizure processes",
      "outcome": "Business expansion, formal employment, and financial development were discouraged or impeded.",
      "date_or_period": "2022 assessment",
      "quantities": null,
      "attribution": "IMF staff assessment",
      "period_fit": "Fits the 2022 structural-policy assessment.",
      "limitations": "This is an institutional outcome and does not by itself establish the ruler's decisions or compliance.",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "methodology_ids": ["5B.4", "5B.6", "5B.10"],
      "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a",
      "locator": "page 30",
      "start_segment_id": "S00009",
      "end_segment_id": "S00011"
    },
    {
      "draft_id": "D0022",
      "intent": "The IMF assessed that corruption undermined public-service provision, organized crime increased transport and insurance costs and discouraged entrepreneurs and business formation, and improved governance could unlock investment and growth potential.",
      "actor": "Mexican governance and security environment",
